cues.zh: 这个概念。

cues.en: To answer that, we have to go back to a discovery made two centuries ago.
cues.zh: 要回答这个问题，我们得回到两个世纪前的一项发现。

cues.en: In the winter of eighteen thirteen, France was being invaded by the armies of Austria,
cues.zh: 1813年冬天，法国正被奥地利、

cues.en: Prussia, and Russia.
cues.zh: 普鲁士和俄罗斯的军队入侵。

cues.en: The son of one of Napoleon's generals was Sadi Carnot,
cues.zh: 拿破仑一位将军的儿子是萨迪·卡诺，

cues.en: a 17 year old student.
cues.zh: 一个17岁的学生。

cues.en: On December 29, he writes a letter to Napoleon to request to join in the fight.
cues.zh: 12月29日，他写信给拿破仑，请求参战。

cues.en: Napoleon,
cues.zh: 拿破仑，

cues.en: preoccupied in battle, never replies.
cues.zh: 忙于战斗，从未回复。

cues.en: But Carnot gets his wish a few months later when Paris is attacked.
cues.zh: 但几个月后巴黎遭到攻击时，卡诺如愿以偿。

cues.en: The students defend a chateau just east of the city,
cues.zh: 学生们守卫着城市东边的一座城堡，

cues.en: but they're no match for the advancing armies and Paris falls after only a day of fighting.
cues.zh: 但他们不是推进军队的对手，巴黎只打了一天就陷落了。

cues.en: Forced to retreat,
cues.zh: 被迫撤退，

cues.en: Carnot is devastated.
cues.zh: 卡诺悲痛欲绝。

cues.en: Seven years later, he goes to visit his father who's fled to Prussia after Napoleon's downfall.
cues.zh: 七年后，他去拜访父亲，父亲在拿破仑倒台后逃到了普鲁士。

cues.en: His father was not only a general, but also a physicist. He wrote an essay on how energy is most efficiently transferred in mechanical systems.
cues.zh: 他的父亲不仅是一位将军，还是一位物理学家。他曾写过一篇关于能量如何在机械系统中最高效传递的论文。

cues.en: When his son comes to visit, they talk at length about the big breakthrough of the time,
cues.zh: 当儿子前去探望时，他们长谈了那个时代的重大突破——

cues.en: steam engines.
cues.zh: 蒸汽机。

cues.en: Steam engines were already being used to power ships, mine ore, and excavate ports.
cues.zh: 当时蒸汽机已经被用来驱动轮船、开采矿石和挖掘港口。

cues.en: And it was clear that the future industrial and military might of nations
cues.zh: 很显然，各国未来的工业与军事实力

cues.en: depended
cues.zh: 都取决于

cues.en: on having the best steam engines.
cues.zh: 谁能拥有最顶尖的蒸汽机。

cues.en: But French designs were falling behind those of other countries like Britain.
cues.zh: 但法国的设计当时已经落后于英国等国。

cues.en: So, Sadi Carnot took it upon himself to figure out why.
cues.zh: 于是，Sadi Carnot 决定亲自查明原因。

cues.en: At the time, even the best steam engines only converted around 3% of thermal energy into useful mechanical work.
cues.zh: 在当时，即便是最先进的蒸汽机，也只能将大约 3% 的热能转化为有用的机械功。

cues.en: If he could improve on that, he could give France a huge advantage
cues.zh: 如果能提高这一效率，他就能让法国获得巨大的优势，

cues.en: and restore its place in the world.
cues.zh: 重塑其世界强国的地位。

cues.en: So he spends the next three years studying heat engines.
cues.zh: 因此，在接下来的三年里，他潜心研究热机。

cues.en: And one of his key insights involves how an ideal heat engine would work, one with no friction and no losses to the environment.
cues.zh: 他的核心见解之一，正是理想热机的工作方式——一种没有摩擦、对环境零损耗的热机。

cues.en: It looks something like this.
cues.zh: 它大概是这样的。

cues.en: Take two really big metal bars, one hot and one cold.
cues.zh: 设想有两根巨大的金属棒，一热一冷。

cues.en: The engine consists of a chamber filled with air where heat can only flow in or out through the bottom.
cues.zh: 这台热机包含一个充满空气的气室，热量只能从底部进出。

cues.en: Inside the chamber is a piston which is connected to a flywheel.
cues.zh: 气室内部有一个连接着飞轮的活塞。

cues.en: The air starts at a temperature just below that of the hotbar.
cues.zh: 空气的初始温度略低于高温金属棒。

cues.en: So first, the hotbar is brought into contact with the chamber. The air inside expands with heat flowing into it to maintain its temperature.
cues.zh: 首先，让高温金属棒接触气室。热量流入内部以维持温度，里面的空气随之膨胀。

cues.en: This pushes the piston up turning the flywheel.
cues.zh: 这推动活塞向上，带动飞轮转动。

cues.en: Next, the hot bar is removed,
cues.zh: 接下来，移走热棒，

cues.en: but the air in the chamber continues to expand.
cues.zh: 但腔内的空气继续膨胀。

cues.en: Except now without heat entering, the temperature decreases.
cues.zh: 只不过现在没有热量进入，温度开始下降。

cues.en: In the ideal case, until it is the temperature of the cold bar.
cues.zh: 在理想情况下，一直降到与冷棒相同的温度。

cues.en: The cold bar is brought into contact with the chamber and the flywheel pushes the piston down.
cues.zh: 让冷棒与腔体接触，飞轮推动活塞向下。

cues.en: And as the air is compressed, heat is transferred into the cold bar.
cues.zh: 随着空气被压缩，热量被传递到冷棒中。

cues.en: The cold bar is removed. The flywheel compresses the gas further increasing its temperature until it is just below that of the hotbar.
cues.zh: 移走冷棒。飞轮继续压缩气体，使其温度升高，直到略低于热棒的温度。

cues.en: Then the hotbar is connected again and the cycle repeats.
cues.zh: 然后再次连接热棒，循环重复。

cues.en: Through this process, heat from the hotbar is converted
cues.zh: 通过这个过程，热棒的热量被转化为

cues.en: into the energy of the flywheel.
cues.zh: 飞轮的动能。

cues.en: And what's interesting to note about Carnot's ideal engine is that it is completely reversible.
cues.zh: 关于卡诺理想热机，有趣的一点是它完全可逆。

cues.en: If you ran the engine in reverse, first the air expands lowering the temperature,
cues.zh: 如果反向运行这个热机，首先空气膨胀，温度降低，

cues.en: then the chamber is brought into contact with the cold bar. The air expands more drawing in heat from the cold bar.
cues.zh: 然后让腔体与冷棒接触。空气继续膨胀，从冷棒中吸收热量。

cues.en: Next, the air is compressed increasing its temperature.
cues.zh: 接下来，空气被压缩，温度升高。

cues.en: The chamber is placed on top of the hot bar and the energy of the flywheel is used to return the heat back into the hot bar.
cues.zh: 将腔体放在热棒上方，利用飞轮的能量把热量送回热棒中。

cues.en: However many cycles were run-in the forward direction,
cues.zh: 无论正向运行了多少个循环，

cues.en: you could run the same number in reverse and at the end, everything would return to its original state with no additional input of energy required.
cues.zh: 你都可以反向运行相同的次数，最终一切都会回到初始状态，无需额外输入能量。

cues.en: So by running an ideal engine,
cues.zh: 所以，运行一台理想热机，

cues.en: nothing really changes. You can always undo what you did.
cues.zh: 实际上什么都不会改变。你总能撤销你做过的操作。

cues.en: So what is the efficiency of this engine? Since it's fully reversible,
cues.zh: 那么这台热机的效率是多少？由于它完全可逆，

cues.en: you might expect the efficiency to be 100%,
cues.zh: 你可能会以为效率是100%，

cues.en: but that is not the case.
cues.zh: 但事实并非如此。

cues.en: Each cycle, the energy of the flywheel increases by the amount of heat flowing into chamber from the hot bar
cues.zh: 每个循环中，飞轮的能量增加量等于从热棒流入腔室的热量

cues.en: minus the heat flowing out of the chamber at the cold bar.
cues.zh: 减去在冷棒处流出腔室的热量。

cues.en: So to calculate the efficiency, we divide this energy by the heat input from the hot bar.
cues.zh: 所以要计算效率，我们把这部分能量除以来自热棒的热量输入。

cues.en: Now, the heat in on the hot side is equal to the work done by the gas on the piston.
cues.zh: 现在，热侧输入的热量等于气体对活塞所做的功。

cues.en: And this will always be greater than the work done by the piston on the gas on the cold side,
cues.zh: 而这总是大于冷侧活塞对气体所做的功，

cues.en: which equals the heat out.
cues.zh: 后者等于输出的热量。

cues.en: And this is because on the hot side, the hot gas exerts a greater pressure on the piston than that same gas when cold.
cues.zh: 这是因为在热侧，热气体对活塞施加的压力比同一气体冷却时更大。

cues.en: To increase the efficiency of the engine, you could increase the temperature of the hot side or decrease the temperature of the cold side or both.
cues.zh: 要提高热机效率，你可以提高热侧温度，或降低冷侧温度，或两者兼施。

cues.en: Lord Kelvin learns of Carnot's ideal heat engine and realizes
cues.zh: 开尔文勋爵了解到卡诺的理想热机，并意识到

cues.en: it could form the basis for an absolute temperature scale.
cues.zh: 它可以构成绝对温标的基础。

cues.en: Imagine that the gas is allowed to expand an extreme amount so much that it cools to the point where all the gas particles effectively stop moving.
cues.zh: 想象一下，让气体膨胀到极大程度，以至于冷却到所有气体粒子实际上都停止运动的地步。

cues.en: Then they would exert no pressure on the piston and it would take no work to compress it on the cold side,
cues.zh: 那么它们对活塞不施加任何压力，在冷侧压缩它也不需要做功，

cues.en: so no heat would be lost.
cues.zh: 因此不会有热量损失。

cues.en: This is the idea of absolute zero
cues.zh: 这就是绝对零度的概念

cues.en: and it would make for a 100%
cues.zh: 它能打造出 100%

cues.en: efficient engine.
cues.zh: 高效的引擎。

cues.en: Using this absolute temperature scale, the Kelvin scale,
cues.zh: 用这个绝对温标，也就是开尔文温标，

cues.en: we can replace the amount of heat in and out with the temperature of the hot and cold side respectively
cues.zh: 我们就能把输入和输出的热量分别替换成热侧和冷侧的温度

cues.en: because they are directly proportional.
cues.zh: 因为它们成正比。

cues.en: So we can express efficiency like this, which we can rewrite like this.
cues.zh: 于是效率可以这样表示，再改写成这样。

cues.en: What we have learned is that the efficiency of an ideal heat engine doesn't depend on the materials or the design of the engine,
cues.zh: 我们学到的是，理想热机的效率并不取决于材料或引擎设计，

cues.en: but fundamentally on the temperatures of the hot and cold sides.
cues.zh: 而是根本上取决于热侧和冷侧的温度。

cues.en: To reach a 100% efficiency, you'd need infinite temperature on the hot side or absolute zero on the cold side, both of which are impossible in practice. So even with no friction or losses to the environment, it's impossible to make a heat engine a 100% efficient. And that's because to return the piston to its original position, you need to dump heat into the cold bar, so not all the energy stays in the flywheel.
cues.zh: 要达到 100% 的效率，热侧需要无限高的温度，或者冷侧达到绝对零度，两者在实际中都不可能。所以即使没有摩擦、没有向环境的热损失，热机也不可能做到 100% 高效。因为要让活塞回到原位，你必须把热量排到冷侧，所以并不是所有能量都留在了飞轮里。

cues.en: Now in Carnot's time, high pressure steam engines could only reach temperatures up to a 160 degrees Celsius.
cues.zh: 在卡诺那个年代，高压蒸汽机最高只能达到 160 摄氏度。

cues.en: So their theoretical maximum efficiency was 32%,
cues.zh: 所以它们的理论最高效率是 32%，

cues.en: but their real efficiency was more like 3%.
cues.zh: 但实际效率只有 3% 左右。

cues.en: That's because real engines experience friction,
cues.zh: 这是因为真实引擎会有摩擦，

cues.en: dissipate heat to the environment, and they don't transfer heat at constant temperatures.
cues.zh: 会向环境散发热量，而且它们不是在恒温下传热的。

cues.en: So for just as much heat going in,
cues.zh: 所以即使输入的热量一样多，

cues.en: less energy ends up in the flywheel.
cues.zh: 最终留在飞轮里的能量却更少。

cues.en: The rest is spread out over the walls of the cylinder, the axle of the flywheel, and is radiated out into the environment.
cues.zh: 其余部分散落在圆柱体的壁上、飞轮的轴上，并向周围环境辐射出去。

cues.en: When energy spreads out like this, it is impossible to get it back.
cues.zh: 当能量这样散开时，就无法再收回了。

cues.en: So this process is irreversible.
cues.zh: 所以这个进程是不可逆的。

cues.en: The total amount of energy didn't change,
cues.zh: 总能量没有改变，

cues.en: but it became less usable.
cues.zh: 但它变得不那么好用了。

cues.en: Energy is most usable when it is concentrated and less usable when it's spread out.
cues.zh: 能量集中时最可用，分散时则不太可用。

cues.en: Decades later, German physicist Rudolf Clausius studies Carnot's engine and he comes up with a way to measure how spread out the energy is.
cues.zh: 几十年后，德国物理学家 Rudolf Clausius 研究了 Carnot 的热机，并想出了一种衡量能量分散程度的方法。

cues.en: He calls this quantity
cues.zh: 他把这个量称为

cues.en: entropy.
cues.zh: 熵。

cues.en: When all the energy is concentrated in the hot bar, that is low entropy.
cues.zh: 当所有能量都集中在热棒上时，那就是低熵。

cues.en: But as the energy spreads to the surroundings, the walls of the chamber and the axle, well, entropy increases.
cues.zh: 但随着能量扩散到周围环境，即腔壁和轴，熵便增加了。

cues.en: This means the same amount of energy is present,
cues.zh: 这意味着能量总量是相同的，

cues.en: but in this more dispersed form, it is less available to do work.
cues.zh: 但以这种更分散的形式存在时，它可用于做功的能量就更少了。

cues.en: Clausius summarizes the first two laws of thermodynamics
cues.zh: 克劳修斯总结了热力学的前两大定律

cues.en: like this.
cues.zh: 像这样。

cues.en: The first, the energy of the universe is constant.
cues.zh: 首先，宇宙的能量是恒定的。

cues.en: And second,
cues.zh: 第二，

cues.en: the entropy of the universe
cues.zh: 宇宙的熵

cues.en: tends to a maximum.
cues.zh: 趋于最大值。

cues.en: In other words, energy spreads out over time.
cues.zh: 换句话说，能量会随时间扩散。

cues.en: The second law is core to so many phenomena in the world. It's why hot things cool down and cool things heat up, why gas expands to fill a container? Why you can't have a perpetual motion machine? Because the amount of usable energy in a closed system is always decreasing.
cues.zh: 第二定律是世上如此多现象的核心。它解释了为什么热的物体会变冷、冷的物体会变热，为什么气体会膨胀充满容器？为什么不可能有永动机？因为封闭系统中可用的能量总是在减少。

cues.en: The most common way to describe entropy is as disorder,
cues.zh: 描述熵最常见的方式是把它看作无序，

cues.en: which makes sense because it is associated with things becoming more mixed,
cues.zh: 这说得通，因为它和事物变得更混杂、

cues.en: and less ordered. But I think the best way to think about entropy is as the tendency of energy to spread out.
cues.zh: 更无序有关。但我认为理解熵最好的方式，是把它看作能量扩散的趋势。

cues.en: So why does energy spread out over time? I mean, most of the laws of physics work exactly the same way forwards or backwards in time.
cues.zh: 那么为什么能量会随时间扩散呢？我的意思是，大多数物理定律在时间正反方向上都是一样的。

cues.en: So how does this clear time dependence arise?
cues.zh: 那么这种明显的时间依赖性是如何产生的？

cues.en: Well, let's consider two small metal bars, one hot and one cold.
cues.zh: 让我们考虑两根小金属棒，一根热，一根冷。

cues.en: For this simple model, we'll consider only eight atoms per bar.
cues.zh: 在这个简单模型中，我们只考虑每根棒八个原子。

cues.en: Each atom vibrates according to the number of energy packets it has. The more packets, the more it vibrates.
cues.zh: 每个原子根据它拥有的能量包数量振动。能量包越多，振动越剧烈。

cues.en: So let's start with seven packets of energy in the left bar and three in the right.
cues.zh: 让我们从左棒有七个能量包、右棒有三个开始。

cues.en: The number of energy packets in each bar is what we'll call a state.
cues.zh: 每根棒中的能量包数量，我们称之为一个状态。

cues.en: First, let's consider just the left bar. It has seven energy packets which are free to move around the lattice.
cues.zh: 首先，我们只看左棒。它有七个能量包，可以在晶格中自由移动。

cues.en: This happens nonstop.
cues.zh: 这不停发生。

cues.en: The energy packets hop randomly from atom to atom giving different configurations of energy,
cues.zh: 能量包随机地从原子跳到原子，形成不同的能量配置，

cues.en: but the total energy stays the same the whole time.
cues.zh: 但总能量始终保持不变。

cues.en: Now, let's bring the cold bar back in with only three packets and touch them together.
cues.zh: 现在，把只有三个能量包的冷棒放回来，让它们接触。

cues.en: The energy packets can now hop around between both bars creating different configurations.
cues.zh: 能量包现在可以在两根棒之间跳跃，形成不同的配置。

cues.en: Each unique configuration is equally likely.
cues.zh: 每种独特的配置都等概率。

cues.en: So what happens if we take a snapshot at one instant in time and see where all the energy packets are?
cues.zh: 那么，如果我们在某一瞬间拍个快照，看看所有能量包在哪里，会发生什么？

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: stop.
cues.zh: 停下。

cues.en: Look at this. Now there are nine energy packets in the left bar and only one in the right bar.
cues.zh: 看这里。现在左侧柱里有九个能量包，而右侧柱里只有一个。

cues.en: So heat has flowed from cold to hot.
cues.zh: 所以热量从冷处流向了热处。

cues.en: Shouldn't that be impossible because it decreases entropy?
cues.zh: 可这难道不是不可能吗？因为熵减少了。

cues.en: Well, this is where Ludwig Boltzmann made an important insight.
cues.zh: 嗯，Ludwig Boltzmann 正是在这里提出了一个重要洞见。

cues.en: Heat flowing from cold to hot is not impossible.
cues.zh: 热量从冷处流向热处并非不可能。

cues.en: It's just improbable.
cues.zh: 只是概率很低。

cues.en: There are 91,520
configurations with nine energy packets in the left bar,
cues.zh: 种构型，其中左侧柱里有九个能量包，

cues.en: with five energy packets in each bar. That is, the energy is more than six times as likely to be evenly spread between the bars.
cues.zh: 种构型，每个柱里有五个能量包。也就是说，能量在两个柱之间均匀分布的可能性要高出六倍多。

cues.en: But if you add up all the possibilities,
cues.zh: 但如果你把所有可能性加起来，

cues.en: find there's still a 10.5%
cues.zh: 会发现仍然有 10.5% 的

cues.en: chance that the left bar ends up with more energy packets than it started.
cues.zh: 概率，左侧柱最终拥有的能量包会比开始时更多。

cues.en: So why don't we observe this happening around us?
cues.zh: 那为什么我们没在身边观察到这种情况呢？

cues.en: Well, watch what happens as we increase the number of atoms to 80 per bar and the energy packets to a 100 with 70 in the left bar and 30 in the right.
cues.zh: 好，看看当我们把每个柱的原子数增加到 80，把能量包增加到 100 个，其中左侧柱 70 个、右侧柱 30 个时，会发生什么。

cues.en: There is now only a point 05%
cues.zh: 现在只有 0.05% 的

cues.en: chance that the left solid ends up hotter than it started.
cues.zh: 概率，左侧固体最终会比开始时更热。

cues.en: And this trend continues as we keep scaling up the system.
cues.zh: 而且随着我们不断扩大系统规模，这个趋势会继续下去。

cues.en: In everyday solids, there are around a 100,000,000,000,000
atoms and even more energy packets.
cues.zh: 原子，能量包甚至更多。

cues.en: So heat flowing from cold to hot is just so unlikely
cues.zh: 所以热量从冷处流向热处实在太不可能

cues.en: that it never happens.
cues.zh: 以至于永远不会发生。

cues.en: Think of it like this Rubik's cube. Right now, it is completely solved, but I'm gonna close my eyes and make some turns at random.
cues.zh: 可以把它想象成这个魔方。现在它是完全复原的，但我要闭上眼睛，随机转动几下。

cues.en: If I keep doing this, it will get further and further from being solved.
cues.zh: 我要是一直这么拧下去，它只会离还原越来越远。

cues.en: But how can I be confident that I'm really messing this cube up? Well, because there's only one way for it to be solved, a few ways for it to be almost solved,
cues.zh: 可我怎么确定我真把它打乱了呢？因为还原它的方式只有一种，接近还原的方式只有几种，

cues.en: and quintillions
cues.zh: 而几乎完全随机的状态

cues.en: of ways for it to be almost entirely random.
cues.zh: 有千千万万亿亿种。

cues.en: Without thought and effort, every turn moves the Rubik's cube from a highly unlikely state, that of it being solved, to a more likely state, a total mess.
cues.zh: 不经思考和努力，每转一下都会让魔方从一个极不可能的状态——也就是还原状态——走向一个更可能的状态，也就是彻底乱掉。

cues.en: So if the natural tendency of energy is to spread out and for things to get messier,
cues.zh: 所以，如果能量的自然倾向是扩散、事物趋于更混乱，

cues.en: then how is it possible to have something like air conditioning,
cues.zh: 那怎么会有空调这种东西，

cues.en: where the cold interior of a house gets cooler and the hot exterior gets hotter?
cues.zh: 让屋内变冷、屋外更热呢？

cues.en: Energy is going from cold to hot,
cues.zh: 能量从冷处流向热处，

cues.en: decreasing the entropy of the house.
cues.zh: 降低了房子的熵。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: this decrease in entropy is only possible
cues.zh: 这种熵的降低之所以可能，

cues.en: by increasing the entropy a greater amount somewhere else.
cues.zh: 是因为在别处让熵增加了更大的量。

cues.en: In this case, at a power plant, the concentrated chemical energy in coal is being released, heating up the power plant in its environment,
cues.zh: 在这个例子里，发电厂把煤里集中的化学能释放出来，加热发电厂及其周围环境，

cues.en: spreading to the turbine, the electric generators, heating the wires all the way to the house, and producing waste heat in the fans and compressor.
cues.zh: 能量传到涡轮机、发电机，一路加热电线直到房子，还在风扇和压缩机里产生废热。

cues.en: Whatever decrease in entropy is achieved at the house is more than paid for by an increase in entropy required to make that happen.
cues.zh: 房子里降低的那点熵，远不足以抵消为实现它而增加的熵。

cues.en: But if total entropy is constantly increasing and anything we do only accelerates that increase,
cues.zh: 但如果总熵一直在增加，而我们做任何事都只会加速这个增加，

cues.en: then how is there any structure left on earth?
cues.zh: 那地球上怎么还会有结构存在呢？

cues.en: How are there hot parts separate from cold parts? How does life exist?
cues.zh: 热的部分和冷的部分怎么会分开？生命是如何存在的？

cues.en: Well, if the earth were a closed system, the energy would spread out completely.
cues.zh: 如果地球是一个封闭系统，能量就会完全扩散开来。

cues.en: Meaning,
cues.zh: 也就是说，

cues.en: all life would cease, everything would decay and mix and eventually reach the same temperature.
cues.zh: 所有生命都会终止，一切都会衰败、混合，最终达到相同的温度。

cues.en: But luckily,
cues.zh: 但幸运的是，

cues.en: Earth is not a closed system
cues.zh: 地球不是一个封闭系统

cues.en: because
cues.zh: 因为

cues.en: we have the sun.
cues.zh: 我们有太阳。

cues.en: What the sun really gives us is a steady stream of low entropy that is concentrated
cues.zh: 太阳真正给我们的，是一股稳定的低熵流，是集中的

cues.en: bundled up energy.
cues.zh: 被束在一起的能量。

cues.en: The energy that we get from the sun is more useful
cues.zh: 我们从太阳获得的能量更有用

cues.en: than the energy we give back. It's more compact, it's more clumped together.
cues.zh: 比我们返还的能量更有用。它更紧凑，更聚拢在一起。

cues.en: Plants capture this energy and use it to grow and create sugars.
cues.zh: 植物捕获这些能量，用来生长并制造糖分。

cues.en: Then animals eat plants and use that energy to maintain their bodies and move around.
cues.zh: 然后动物吃植物，用这些能量维持身体并四处活动。

cues.en: Bigger animals get their energy by eating smaller animals and so on.
cues.zh: 更大的动物通过吃更小的动物来获取能量，以此类推。

cues.en: And each step of the way, the energy becomes more spread out. Okay. Interesting. Yeah. Oh, wow. I did not know that. There you go. Ultimately,
cues.zh: 而每一步，能量都变得更加分散。好。有意思。是啊。哦，哇。我之前不知道这个。这就对了。最终，

cues.en: all the energy that reaches earth from the sun is converted into thermal energy and then it's radiated back into space.
cues.zh: 所有从太阳到达地球的能量都会转化为热能，然后辐射回太空。

cues.en: But in fact it's the same amount.
cues.zh: 但事实上，总量是相同的。

cues.en: I know this is a... You you do know this is... I'm I'm a PhD physicist. Okay. Okay. Anyway... I trust you.
cues.zh: 我知道这是……你你知道这是……我是物理学博士。好吧。好吧。总之……我信你。

cues.en: The increase in entropy can be seen in the relative number of photons arriving at and leaving the earth.
cues.zh: 熵的增加可以从到达和离开地球的光子相对数量上看出来。

cues.en: For each photon received from the sun,
cues.zh: 每接收一个来自太阳的光子，

cues.en: 20 photons are emitted.
cues.zh: 就会发射出20个光子。

cues.en: And everything that happens on earth, plants growing, trees falling,
cues.zh: 地球上发生的一切，植物生长、树木倒下，

cues.en: herds stampeding,
cues.zh: 兽群奔逃，

cues.en: hurricanes and tornadoes,
cues.zh: 飓风和龙卷风，

cues.en: people eating, sleeping and breathing,
cues.zh: 人们吃饭、睡觉和呼吸，

cues.en: all of it happens in the process of converting fewer higher energy photons into 20 times as many lower energy photons.
cues.zh: 这一切都发生在将较少的高能光子转化为20倍之多的低能光子的过程中。

cues.en: Without a source of concentrated energy and a way to discard the spread out energy,
cues.zh: 如果没有集中的能量来源和释放分散能量的方式，

cues.en: life on earth would not be possible.
cues.zh: 地球上的生命就不可能存在。

cues.en: It has even been suggested that life itself may be a consequence of the second law of thermodynamics.
cues.zh: 甚至有人认为，生命本身可能就是热力学第二定律的结果。

cues.en: If the universe tends toward maximum entropy,
cues.zh: 如果宇宙趋向于最大熵，

cues.en: then life offers a way to accelerate that natural tendency
cues.zh: 那么生命提供了一种加速这一自然趋势的方式，

cues.en: because life is spectacularly
cues.zh: 因为生命极其

cues.en: good at converting low entropy into high entropy.
cues.zh: 擅长将低熵转化为高熵。

cues.en: For example, the surface layer of seawater produces between
cues.zh: 例如，海水表层在

cues.en: more entropy
cues.zh: 之间产生更多熵，

cues.en: when cyanobacteria
cues.zh: 当蓝细菌

cues.en: and other organic matter is present than when it's not.
cues.zh: 和其他有机物存在时，比不存在时更多。

cues.en: Jeremy England takes this one step further. He's proposed that if there is a constant stream of clumped up energy,
cues.zh: Jeremy England更进一步。他提出，如果存在持续不断的聚集能量流，

cues.en: this could favor structures that dissipate that energy.
cues.zh: 这可能会有利于耗散该能量的结构。

cues.en: And over time, this results in better and better energy dissipators
cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，这会产生越来越好的能量耗散体，

cues.en: eventually resulting in life.
cues.zh: 最终产生生命。

cues.en: Or in his own words, you start with a random clump of atoms and if you shine light on it for long enough, it should not be so surprising that you get a plant.
cues.zh: 或者用他自己的话说，你从一堆随机聚集的原子开始，如果你照射光足够长时间，得到一株植物就不那么令人惊讶了。

cues.en: So life on earth survives on the low entropy from the sun.
cues.zh: 所以地球上的生命依靠来自太阳的低熵而存活。

cues.en: But then, where did the sun get its low entropy?
cues.zh: 可太阳的低熵又是从哪来的？

cues.en: The answer is the universe.
cues.zh: 答案是宇宙。

cues.en: If we know that the total entropy of the universe is increasing with time,
cues.zh: 如果我们知道宇宙的总熵随时间增加，

cues.en: then it was lower entropy yesterday
cues.zh: 那么昨天的熵就更低，

cues.en: and even lower entropy the day before that and so on all the way back to the big bang.
cues.zh: 前天的熵还要更低，以此类推，一直追溯到宇宙大爆炸。

cues.en: So right after the big bang,
cues.zh: 所以就在大爆炸之后，

cues.en: that is when the entropy was lowest.
cues.zh: 那时熵是最低的。

cues.en: This is known as the past hypothesis.
cues.zh: 这被称为过去假设。

cues.en: It doesn't explain why the entropy was low, just that it must have been that way for the universe to unfold as it has.
cues.zh: 它并没有解释熵为什么低，只是说宇宙要如此演化，就必须是那样。

cues.en: But the early universe was hot, dense, and almost completely uniform. I mean, everything was mixed and the temperature was basically the same everywhere,
cues.zh: 但早期宇宙又热又密，而且几乎完全均匀。我的意思是，一切都混在一起，各处温度基本一致，

cues.en: varying by at most point 001%.
cues.zh: 差异最多只有 0.001%。

cues.en: So how is this low entropy?
cues.zh: 那这怎么算低熵呢？

cues.en: Well, the thing we've left out is gravity.
cues.zh: 我们漏掉的一个因素是引力。

cues.en: Gravity tends to clump matter together.
cues.zh: 引力倾向于把物质聚拢在一起。

cues.en: So taking gravity into account, having matter all spread out like this would be an extremely unlikely state,
cues.zh: 所以把引力考虑进来，物质这样均匀散布其实是一个极不可能的状态，

cues.en: and that is why it's low entropy.
cues.zh: 这就是为什么它是低熵。

cues.en: Over time, as the universe expanded and cooled,
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，宇宙膨胀并冷却，

cues.en: matter started to clump together in more dense regions.
cues.zh: 物质开始聚集成更密集的区域。

cues.en: And in doing so, enormous
cues.zh: 在此过程中，巨大的

cues.en: amounts of potential energy were turned into kinetic energy.
cues.zh: 势能转化成了动能。

cues.en: And this energy could also be used, like how water flowing downhill can power a turbine.
cues.zh: 这种能量也可以被利用，就像水流下山能驱动涡轮机一样。

cues.en: But as bits of matter started hitting each other, some of their energy was converted into heat.
cues.zh: 但随着物质粒子开始相互碰撞，其中一部分能量转化成了热。

cues.en: So the amount of useful energy decreased,
cues.zh: 于是可用能量减少了，

cues.en: thereby increasing
cues.zh: 从而增加了

cues.en: entropy.
cues.zh: 熵。

cues.en: Over time, the useful energy was used.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，有用的能量被消耗掉了。

cues.en: In doing so, stars, planets, galaxies and life were formed,
cues.zh: 在这个过程中，恒星、行星、星系和生命得以形成，

cues.en: increasing entropy all along.
cues.zh: 而熵始终在增加。

cues.en: The universe started with around 10 to the 88 Boltzmann
cues.zh: 宇宙起始时大约有10的88次方个玻尔兹曼常数

cues.en: constants worth of entropy.
cues.zh: 那么多的熵。

cues.en: Nowadays, all the stars in the observable universe have about 9.5
cues.zh: 如今，可观测宇宙中所有的恒星大约有9.5

cues.en: times 10 to the 80. The interstellar and intergalactic medium combined have almost 10 times more,
cues.zh: 乘以10的80次方。星际介质和星系际介质加起来差不多是它的10倍，

cues.en: but still only a fraction of the early universe.
cues.zh: 但仍然只是早期宇宙的一小部分。

cues.en: A lot more is contained in neutrinos and in photons of the cosmic microwave background.
cues.zh: 更多的熵存在于中微子和宇宙微波背景的光子中。

cues.en: Jacob Beckenstein proposed another source of entropy,
cues.zh: 雅各布·贝肯斯坦提出了另一种熵的来源，

cues.en: black holes.
cues.zh: 黑洞。

cues.en: He suggested that the entropy of a black hole should be proportional to its surface area. So as a black hole grows, its entropy increases.
cues.zh: 他提出黑洞的熵应该与其表面积成正比。所以当黑洞变大时，它的熵也会增加。

cues.en: Famous physicists thought the idea was nonsense
cues.zh: 著名物理学家认为这个想法是无稽之谈，

cues.en: and for good reason. According to classical thermodynamics,
cues.zh: 而且有充分的理由。根据经典热力学，

cues.en: if black holes have entropy,
cues.zh: 如果黑洞有熵，

cues.en: then they should also have a temperature.
cues.zh: 那么它们也应该有温度。

cues.en: But if they have temperatures, they should emit radiation
cues.zh: 但如果它们有温度，就应该辐射能量，

cues.en: and not be black after all.
cues.zh: 终究不会是黑的。

cues.en: The person who set out to prove Beckenstein wrong was Stephen Hawking.
cues.zh: 立志证明贝肯斯坦错了的人是斯蒂芬·霍金。

cues.en: But to his surprise, his results showed that black holes do emit radiation,
cues.zh: 但令他惊讶的是，他的结果表明黑洞确实会辐射，

cues.en: now known as Hawking radiation,
cues.zh: 如今被称为霍金辐射，

cues.en: and they do have a temperature.
cues.zh: 而且它们确实有温度。

cues.en: The black hole at the center of the Milky Way has a temperature of about a hundred trillionth of a Kelvin,
cues.zh: 银河系中心的黑洞温度大约为一万亿分之一开尔文，

cues.en: emitting radiation that is far too weak to detect, so still pretty black.
cues.zh: 发出的辐射太弱而无法探测，所以看起来还是相当黑的。

cues.en: But Hawking confirmed that black holes have entropy and Beckenstein was right.
cues.zh: 但霍金证实了黑洞确实有熵，贝肯斯坦是对的。

cues.en: Hawking was able to refine Beckenstein's
cues.zh: Hawking得以完善Beckenstein的

cues.en: proposal and determine just how much entropy they have.
cues.zh: 设想，并确定了它们究竟有多少熵。

cues.en: The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way has about 10 to the 91 Boltzmann constants of entropy.
cues.zh: 银河系中心的超大质量黑洞大约有10的91次方个玻尔兹曼常数的熵。

cues.en: That is a thousand times as much as the early observable universe
cues.zh: 这比早期可观测宇宙多一千倍，

cues.en: and 10 times more than all the other particles combined.
cues.zh: 比所有其他粒子加起来还多10倍。

cues.en: And that is just one black hole. All black holes together account for three times 10 to the 104
cues.zh: 而这只是一个黑洞。所有黑洞加起来贡献了3乘以10的104次方

cues.en: Boltzmann constants worth of entropy.
cues.zh: 个玻尔兹曼常数的熵。

cues.en: So almost all the entropy of the universe
cues.zh: 所以宇宙几乎所有的熵

cues.en: is tied up in black holes.
cues.zh: 都锁在黑洞里。

cues.en: That means the early universe only had about point 00000000003%
cues.zh: 这意味着早期宇宙只有大约0.00000000003%

cues.en: of the entropy it has now.
cues.zh: 的现在的熵。

cues.en: So the entropy was low and everything that happens in the universe like planetary systems forming, galaxies merging,
cues.zh: 所以熵很低，宇宙中发生的一切，比如行星系统形成、星系合并、

cues.en: asteroids crashing,
cues.zh: 小行星碰撞、

cues.en: stars dying to life itself flourishing,
cues.zh: 恒星死亡、生命繁荣，

cues.en: all of that can happen because the entropy of the universe was low and it has been increasing.
cues.zh: 所有这些能发生，是因为宇宙的熵很低并且在增加。

cues.en: And it all happens only in one direction. We never see an asteroid uncrash
cues.zh: 而且一切都只朝一个方向发生。我们从未见过小行星“反碰撞”

cues.en: or a planetary system unmix into the cloud of dust and gas that made it up. There is a clear difference between going to the past and the future
cues.zh: 或行星系统“反混合”回形成它的尘埃和气体云。过去和未来之间有明显的区别，

cues.en: and that difference comes from entropy.
cues.zh: 这个区别来自熵。

cues.en: The fact that we are going from unlikely to more likely states is why there is an arrow of time.
cues.zh: 我们从不太可能的状态走向更可能的状态，这就是时间之箭存在的原因。

cues.en: This is expected to continue until eventually
cues.zh: 这一过程预计会持续下去，直到最终

cues.en: the energy gets spread out so completely that nothing interesting will ever happen again.
cues.zh: 能量彻底均匀散布开来，再也不会有任何有趣的事情发生。

cues.en: This is the heat death of the universe.
cues.zh: 这就是宇宙的热寂。

cues.en: In the distant future, more than ten to the hundred years from now, after the last black hole has evaporated,
cues.zh: 在遥远的未来，距今超过十的一百次方年之后，当最后一个黑洞蒸发殆尽，

cues.en: the universe will be in its most probable state.
cues.zh: 宇宙将处于其最可能的状态。

cues.en: Now, even on large scales, you would not be able to tell the difference between time moving forwards or backwards.
cues.zh: 那时，即便在宏观尺度上，你也分辨不出时间是向前还是向后流动。

cues.en: The arrow of time itself would disappear.
cues.zh: 时间之箭本身也将消失。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: it sounds like entropy is this awful thing that leads us inevitably towards the dullest outcome imaginable.
cues.zh: 听起来熵是个可怕的东西，不可避免地把我们引向最乏味的结果。

cues.en: But just because maximum entropy has low complexity does not mean that low entropy has maximum complexity. It's actually more like this tea and milk. I mean, holding it like this is not very interesting. But as I pour the milk in, the two start to mix
cues.zh: 但最大熵对应低复杂度，并不意味着低熵就对应最大复杂度。其实更像是这杯茶和牛奶。我是说，这样端着它没什么意思。但当我倒入牛奶，两者开始混合

cues.en: and these beautiful patterns emerge.
cues.zh: 就浮现出这些美丽的图案。

cues.en: They arise in an instant and before you know it, they're gone back to being featureless.
cues.zh: 它们瞬间出现，转眼之间又消失，重归平淡无奇。

cues.en: Both low and high entropy are low in complexity.
cues.zh: 低熵和高熵都对应低复杂度。

cues.en: It's in the middle where complex structures appear and thrive.
cues.zh: 复杂结构正是在中间地带出现并繁荣。

cues.en: And since that's where we find ourselves,
cues.zh: 既然我们正身处其中，

cues.en: let's make use of the low entropy we've got while we can.
cues.zh: 那就趁我们还能利用手中的低熵，好好加以利用吧。

cues.zh: 有了合适的工具，我们几乎能理解一切——从一杯逐渐冷却的茶，到整个宇宙的演化。
